findings.description: The security group allows inbound TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on a publicly addressable instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploitation attempts.

Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 serving cleartext HTTP traffic, and egress is unrestricted to all destinations on all protocols, which permits data exfiltration and command-and-control traffic from a compromised host.

The user_data script exports a static AWS access key ID and secret access key in cleartext. EC2 user data is retrievable via the instance metadata service by any process or SSRF vector on the host, leaking long-lived IAM credentials.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled. Combined with the credentials stored in user_data and a public-facing web server, a single SSRF flaw allows retrieval of those secrets and any role credentials.
The instance defines no root_block_device with encrypted = true, so the root volume is created without EBS encryption at rest.

The instance is launched in a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and routed directly to an internet gateway, placing it on the public internet with no load balancer, bastion, or private-subnet segmentation.
The EBS data volume does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key, so data written to the attached disk is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted EBS volume, so the snapshot data is also unencrypted at rest and can be shared or restored without key control.
The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, leaving network telemetry stored unencrypted.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, ACL, or bucket policy is defined for the flow log bucket, so nothing prevents a later public ACL or policy from exposing sensitive network flow records.
The bucket has no policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, permitting cleartext HTTP access to stored flow logs.

findings.issue_category: Forced destroy on audit log bucket
findings.description: force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all archived VPC flow logs to be deleted with the bucket, undermining the integrity and availability of security audit evidence.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP address by default, removing the network boundary for any future workload placed here.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP address by default, exposing workloads directly to the internet via the attached default route.

Both subnets are associated with a single route table carrying a 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway, so the VPC provides no private tier and no defence-in-depth network segmentation for backend workloads.
